'''Larry Vernon Hedges''' is a researcher in [[statistical methods]] for [[meta-analysis]] and [[evaluation]] of [[education policy]]. He is Professor of Statistics and Education and Social Policy, Institute for Policy Research, [[Northwestern University]]. Previously, he was the Stella M. Rowley Distinguished Service Professor of Education, Sociology, Psychology, and Public Policy Studies at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ipr.northwestern.edu/faculty-experts/fellows/hedges.html |title=Larry V. Hedges |publisher=[[Northwestern University]] |access-date=2013-05-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.statistics.northwestern.edu/people/larry-hedges.html |title=Department of Statistics: Larry Hedges |publisher=Northwestern University |date=2009-05-19 |access-date=2010-05-16}}</ref> He is a member of the [[National Academy of Education]] and a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], the [[American Educational Research Association]], the [[American Psychological Association]], and the [[American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{citation|title=Obama taps Northwestern U. prof Larry Hedges for education panel|first=Lynn|last=Sweet|newspaper=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|date=October 19, 2011|url=http://blogs.suntimes.com/sweet/2011/10/obama_taps_northwestern_univer.html}}.</ref> In 2018, he received the [[Yidan Prize|Yidan Prize for Education Research]], one of the world's largest education prizes, which carries an award of HK$30 million (about US$3.9 million).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://yidanprize.org/laureates/larry-hedges|title=Larry V. Hedges|website=Yidan Prize Foundation|access-date=4 Jun 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.northwestern.edu/faculty-accolades/awards-and-medals/yidan-prize.html|title=Yidan Prize|publisher=[[Northwestern University]]|access-date=4 Jun 2026}}</ref>

He has authored a number of articles and books on statistical methods for [[meta-analysis]], which is the use of statistical methods for combining results from different studies. He also suggested several estimators for [[effect size]]s and derived their properties. He carried out research on the relation of resources available to schools and student achievement, most notably the relation between class size and achievement.

==Hedges' <i>g</i>==
In 1981, Hedges published a paper describing the unbiased standardized mean difference, the [[Effect_size#Hedges'_g | <i>g</i> statistic]].<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://doi.org/10.3102/10769986006002107 | doi=10.3102/10769986006002107 | title=Distribution Theory for Glass's Estimator of Effect size and Related Estimators | date=1981 | last1=Hedges | first1=Larry V. | journal=Journal of Educational Statistics | volume=6 | issue=2 | pages=107–128 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> "It turns out that [Cohen's] <i>d</i> has a slight bias, tending to overestimate the absolute value of  in small samples. This bias can be removed by a simple correction that yields an unbiased estimate of, with the unbiased estimate sometimes called Hedges’ <i>g</i>."<ref>Borenstein, Michael, Larry V. Hedges, Julian P. T. Higgins, and Hannah R. Rothstein. 2009. Introduction to Meta-Analysis. Wiley. ISBN 9780470057247</ref>
